_about: Monster families (MONSTER_FAMILIES_DESIGN.md, docs/systems/monster_families_v2_design.md). Each monster's `family` is in monsters.json; this file holds every number the system uses. Tier N needs the Nth number in `thresholds` of DIFFERENT kinds studied; a keystone (a boss, a mini-boss, a seal demon, a monster with proper_noun, or one in the family's `keystones`) counts `keystone_weight` kinds. Abilities are data: `effect` is a primitive in src/family_edges.py and `params` its numbers; `also` adds more parts to one technique. Nothing here scales by floor. `field_note`: one fact-checked piece of folklore per tier (sources: docs/systems/monster_family_field_notes_sources.md); an empty note is hidden.
_full_lore_tier: How much the hero is told of a creature he sees (family_lore.knowledge, src/tells.py): a kind he studied, or whose page was opened, is fully known; so is every kind of a family at this tier (Lore). Below it, Recognise and Forewarned tell him what the family's creatures can do, but not how to beat them, and their Bestiary pages keep their weaknesses hidden.
tier_messages: You know {kin} now. You will recognise every one of them on sight, and know what each can do.
You know the signs of {kin} now. You will sense them when you reach a floor.
popup_leads: You have learned how ordinary people kept {kin} away, and what every one of them fears.
You have learned how a hunter takes {kin}.
tier_chronicle: Took apart enough of {kin} to know the rest of them on sight.
Know the signs {kin} leave on a stair. Can smell them coming.
Learned the old folk ways of keeping {kin} off. They work.
Learned how a hunter takes {kin}. Hunting them now.
Took apart so many of {kin}, I know where each one breaks.

restless_dead.name: The Restless Dead
restless_dead.blurb: The restless dead would not lie quiet in the earth, and they walk as bone and dried flesh at the bidding of a will that is not their own. They feel no pain and yield no ground, and they bring with them all the sicknesses of the grave.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Tales of the walking dead are very ancient, for already in the Epic of Gilgamesh the goddess Ishtar threatened to smash the gates of the underworld and bring up the dead to devour the living.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: When Thorolf Lame-Foot had died, as Eyrbyggja saga tells, every bird that lighted upon his grave fell dead, and the sheep perished in the valley, so that his neighbours knew that he walked.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The smell of the grave hangs upon the stair, for the restless dead walk this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Mourners in Scotland used to lay a wooden platter of salt and earth upon the breast of the dead. The antiquary John Brand recorded that the salt stood for the undying spirit, and that it kept the Devil from the body.

abilities.name: Grave-Salt
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their paralysis, disease and life drain, and their disease lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Grave-Salt: {The} reaches for you with cold, dead fingers, but the salt in your pocket crackles, and {his} grip slides harmlessly away.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Grettir the Strong, as his saga relates, wrestled with the draugr Glámr and cut off his head. Afterward he and the farmer burned the body to cold coals, and they buried the ashes far from any path of men.

abilities.name: Bonebreaker
abilities.text: Your blows hit 6% harder when they strike what the dead fear: the weaknesses on their page.
abilities.trigger_msg: Bonebreaker! You know where the dead are brittle, and there your blow falls. {The} cracks and splinters beneath it!

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: The drowned men of Fróðá, says Eyrbyggja saga, came dripping each night to sit beside the fire, until Kjartan held a court at the door and charged the dead with trespass, and they heard the judgment and departed.

abilities.name: Turn the Dead
abilities.text: A blow at chain 12 or more sends every lesser restless dead in sight fleeing for 6 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Turn the Dead! You raise your hand and speak the old words, and the dead around you shrink back in fear.

ghosts.name: Ghosts and Shades
ghosts.blurb: When the body is gone, something may remain that will not depart from the world. Steel passes through most of these ghosts, and their touch steals away warmth and courage before it steals life.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Pliny the Younger told one of the oldest of ghost stories, of a phantom in chains that haunted a house in Athens until the philosopher Athenodorus dug where it had vanished, found bones in chains, and gave them a proper burial.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: The folk of Wales told of the corpse candle, a light that glided between the churchyard and the house of the dying. In the England of Shakespeare it was said that whenever a candle burned blue, a spirit was near.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The candle-flames lean the wrong way, for ghosts drift on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Mourners in Japan are given a little bag of salt, to cleanse themselves before they go home from a funeral, and in Europe the old folk believed that an iron fence about a graveyard held the dead within it.

abilities.name: Iron and Salt
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their fear and life drain, and their draining no longer heals them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Iron and Salt: {The}'s icy hold settles over you, until it breaks against the cold iron at your belt and you shake yourself free!

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Among the Gaels the second sight was named an dà shealladh, the two sights. Martin Martin wrote in 1703 that when a seer beheld a shroud about any person death was coming, and the higher it had risen, the sooner it would come.

abilities.name: Second Sight
abilities.text: Invisible ghosts within 3 tiles show to you as a faint shimmer you can strike.
abilities.trigger_msg: Second Sight: the air {where} grows suddenly cold and your skin prickles, for you see what the living cannot: {true_a}, drifting toward you!

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Jan Tregeagle was a harsh steward in life, and the legend of Cornwall says that his ghost was laid at last by setting him to empty Dozmary Pool with a limpet shell, so that he should be busy until Judgment Day.

abilities.name: Lay the Ghost
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, your blows ignore their resistances, as if your weapon were blessed.
abilities.trigger_msg: Lay the Ghost! You strike with the old words on your lips, and your blow bites {the} as if your weapon were blessed.

vampires_liches.name: Vampires and Liches
vampires_liches.blurb: These are the dead who have kept their minds and their hunger. Each of them cheated the grave by its own choice, through blood or through sorcery, and keeps its death hidden away in some secret place.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The dread of vampires spread through Europe from the reports of the Austrian army. In 1732 the surgeon Johann Flückinger recorded that villagers of Serbia had staked the dead soldier Arnold Paole, and swore that the corpse groaned and bled.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Villagers who sought the grave of a vampire would lead a black stallion through the churchyard, or a white one in Albania, and mark where it balked. They took holes in the earth of a grave for another sign.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair smells of iron and old roses, for a vampire or a lich keeps court here.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Upon St. Andrew's Eve, when the folk of Romania held that the strigoi were most abroad, each household smeared garlic on its doors and windows, and the young people sat up all night to guard the heads of garlic.

abilities.name: Garlic and Ash
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their life drain and paralysis, and their bite no longer heals them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Garlic and Ash: {The} fixes you with {his} stare, but the garlic at your throat makes {him} flinch, and {his} hold on you is broken.

also.trigger_msg: Garlic and Ash: {The} sinks {his} teeth in, then recoils, spitting. Your garlic-soaked blood cannot heal {him}!

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Country folk of eastern Europe would scatter poppy seed, millet or sand upon the grave of a suspected vampire, for they believed that it must count every grain and would be all the night at the task.

abilities.name: Hunter's Patience
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Hunter's Patience: you have hunted this kind before, and so you breathe slowly and take your time. You have longer to answer in this fight.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: The hunters of vampires chose with care the wood of the stake, which was ash in Russia and the Baltic lands and hawthorn in Serbia. At Sozopol in Bulgaria, in 2012, archaeologists found two medieval skeletons pinned through the chest with rods of iron.

abilities.name: Stake Through the Heart
abilities.text: At chain 18 or more, a lesser vampire or lich below 15% health dies outright: no mist, no rising. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Stake Through the Heart! You drive the point home, and {the} crumbles into a heap of ash.

demons.name: Demons and Devils
demons.blurb: Out of the Pit come creatures of every degree, from the least tormentor to the princes of Hell, and all of them burn and lie and cloud the mind. Yet every people that met them has written down some way to send them back.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Our word demon descends from the Greek daimon, which was a spirit that might help or harm. Socrates declared that a daimonion, an inward voice, held him back whenever he was about to go astray.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Prints like those of hooves appeared in the fresh snow of Devon on a February night in 1855, running for many miles over the fields and even over rooftops and high walls, and some said that Satan himself had walked there.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Brimstone taints the stair, for something from the Pit has climbed this far.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: The Lesser Key of Solomon, a grimoire of the 17th century, bids the conjurer stand within a nine-foot circle written about with holy names, and compel the spirit that he calls to appear in a triangle outside it.

abilities.name: Circle of Salt
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their burning and confusion, and their burning lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Circle of Salt: {The}'s dark power washes toward you, but you scatter a ring of salt about your feet, and it cannot cross the line.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: The Gospel of Mark relates that Jesus asked the name of a spirit that possessed a man. It answered 'Legion, for we are many,' and he sent the spirits into a herd of swine, which rushed down into the sea.

abilities.name: True Names
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder.
abilities.trigger_msg: True Names: you call {the} by {his} true name. {He} flinches as if struck, and your blow lands the harder.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: It is written in the Book of Revelation that an angel came down with the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain, and bound Satan, the dragon, and cast him in and sealed it for a thousand years.

abilities.name: Banishment
abilities.text: At chain 18 or more, a lesser demon below 15% health is cast back into the Pit. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Banishment! You speak the words of binding, and {the} howls as {he} is dragged back down into the Pit.

dragons.name: Dragons and Wyrms
dragons.blurb: Dragons are great serpents, winged or wingless, whose age is past all counting and whose greed is past all reason. Their breath is as a storm and their scales are as armour, yet every one of them has a weak place somewhere.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: A huge skull was dug from a quarry near Klagenfurt in Austria in 1335, and the people took it for a dragon's and made it the model for the head of their dragon statue, though it was in truth that of a woolly rhinoceros.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: The wrath of the dragon in Beowulf was kindled by a theft, for a runaway slave stole a golden cup from its hoard. That same night the wyrm awoke and burned the halls of the Geats, and Beowulf's own among them.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair is scorched and smells of gold, for a wyrm lairs on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Old King Beowulf knew that a shield of linden wood would burn, and so he bade a shield be forged all of iron before he went out to fight the dragon.

abilities.name: Dragon-Ward
abilities.text: Their fire, cold and poison hurt you 5% less, and you get +1 on saving throws against their burning, freezing and poison.
abilities.trigger_msg: Dragon-Ward: {The} breathes, and you turn your shoulder into the blast as the old songs teach. It still burns, but far less.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Sigurd lay hidden in a pit, as the Völsunga saga tells, and drove his sword to the hilt beneath Fafnir's left shoulder. It was a bearded stranger, Odin in disguise, who had counselled him to dig other pits for the blood.

abilities.name: The Soft Belly
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder: Sigurd struck Fafnir from below.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Soft Belly! You stoop low and strike up into the soft scales of {the}'s belly.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Bilbo, as Tolkien tells in The Hobbit, spied a bare patch in the hollow of Smaug's left breast, and a thrush bore the news to Bard, who sent his last arrow home to that very place.

abilities.name: The Missing Scale
abilities.text: At chain 12 or more, your blow ignores a dragon's scales and resistances, even Fafnir's.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Missing Scale! You spy the one bare patch in {the}'s armour, and your blow drives straight into it.

giants.name: Giants and Trolls
giants.blurb: Giants have been the enemies of gods and men since the world was young, huge, strong and hard to kill. Their danger is in their size, yet the tales agree that the bigger they are, the harder they fall.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The Greeks believed that none but the one-eyed Cyclopes could have raised the walls of Mycenae and Tiryns, whose smallest stone, said Pausanias, two mules could not shift, and such walls are still called Cyclopean by archaeologists.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Giants and trolls hated the sound of church bells, said the farmers of Denmark, and great lone boulders were the stones they had thrown. A giantess of Langeland hurled the greatest of all, Damestenen, at Svindinge church, but her cast fell short.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Giants walk this floor, and the stair shakes under their tread.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: David was but a shepherd boy, as the Book of Samuel tells, when he put off the armour of King Saul and chose five smooth stones from the brook, and with a single stone from his sling he felled the giant Goliath.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: a giant is big but slow, and so you keep your nerve and take your time. You have longer to answer in this fight.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: A wedding party of trolls, by the legend of Norway, made merry all night in Romsdal until the sunrise came upon them and turned them all to stone. Two peaks of Trolltindene are called the Bride and the Groom even now.

abilities.name: Fire and Dawn
abilities.text: Your blows stop their regeneration for 3 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Fire and Dawn: you sear {the}'s wound with fire, so that it stops closing.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Jack the Giant Killer won his name in Cornwall, as the English tale has it, for he dug a deep pit and drew the giant Cormoran into it with a blast upon his horn, and there he slew him.

abilities.name: The Bigger They Are
abilities.text: At chain 5 or more, your weapon hits them 5% harder, and 8% harder against a giant that fills more than one tile.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Bigger They Are! You smite {the} upon the knee, and the whole giant staggers.

goblinkin.name: Goblins and Orcs
goblinkin.blurb: The warbands of the tunnels are a people who live by raiding and by the greatness of their numbers. They are bold in company and cowardly when alone, and they lay traps for all who walk without looking.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Tolkien drew the word orc out of Old English, for the Beowulf poet numbered the orcneas, which may mean 'demon-corpses', among the monstrous brood of Cain, beside the giants and the elves.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: The tin miners of Cornwall used to hear the knockers, little spirits of the mine, tapping within the rock. Some said that the knocking led to rich ore, and others that it gave warning of a cave-in.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Crude marks are scored upon the stair, for a goblin warband holds this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Curdie the miner's boy, in George MacDonald's The Princess and the Goblin, drove back the goblins by singing rhymes, which they hated, and by stamping upon their soft feet, for that is a goblin's one weak spot.

abilities.name: Break Their Nerve
abilities.text: When you kill one, each lesser goblin or orc in sight may lose its nerve and flee for 4 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Break Their Nerve! Your blow lands with a terrible crack, and the goblins nearby begin to waver and back away.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Lizzie, in Christina Rossetti's poem Goblin Market, stood fast while the goblin men crushed their enchanted fruit against her face, and never opened her lips, so that she might bear the juice home and save her sister Laura.

abilities.name: Trap-Wise
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their fear and bleeding, and their ambushers never catch you unawares.
abilities.trigger_msg: Trap-Wise: you perceive the goblins' trick a moment before it springs, and step clear in good time.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: The Great Goblin howled with rage, in Tolkien's The Hobbit, at the sight of Orcrist, which goblins call Biter, and when Gandalf cut him down with Glamdring, which they call Beater, his soldiers fled shrieking.

abilities.name: Your Name Is Known
abilities.text: Lesser goblins and orcs flee from you on sight.
abilities.trigger_msg: Your Name Is Known: the goblins see who you are, and they shriek and scatter in every direction!

mortals.name: Mortal Foes
mortals.blurb: Men and women have come down into the dark of their own will, to rob, to worship or to kill for pay. They bleed as you do and they think as you do, and for that reason no other foe is so hard to foretell.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Our word assassin comes down from the Nizari Ismailis of the castle of Alamut in Persia, whom their enemies named hashishin. It was Marco Polo who spread abroad the tales of their master, the Old Man of the Mountain.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: A robber once set a chalk mark on the door of Ali Baba, that the Forty Thieves might find it by night. But the clever slave girl Morgiana saw it, and she chalked the same mark upon the doors of all the neighbours.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Bootprints and a cold campfire mark the stair: armed men and women walk this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Autolycus, master of thieves in the myths of Greece, could alter the look of the cattle that he stole, until Sisyphus set letters of lead in the hooves of his herd, and the hoofprints accused Autolycus by name.

abilities.name: Read Their Hands
abilities.text: The thieves among them can never steal from you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Read Their Hands: {The}'s hand creeps toward your purse, but you have seen it coming, and you catch the wrist and twist it away.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: The bailiff Gessler, as the Swiss tell, made William Tell shoot an apple from the head of his own son. Tell pierced it with one arrow, and then confessed that the second in his quiver had been meant for Gessler.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: you have fought such foes before, and you know their tricks of old. You have longer to answer in this fight.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Lancelot overcame three knights who had set upon Sir Kay, as Malory tells in Le Morte d'Arthur, and he spared them upon this condition, that each should go to the court of King Arthur and yield himself to Queen Guinevere.

abilities.name: Yield!
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, a lesser foe below half health surrenders, throws down the purse and runs.
abilities.trigger_msg: Yield! {The} has had enough, gives up the fight and runs for it!

fair_folk.name: The Fair Folk
fair_folk.blurb: The Fair Folk are the hidden people of the mounds and the deep woods, very beautiful and very perilous, and never wholly honest. They bargain and they bewitch, and they keep every promise exactly as it was worded.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The Irish and the Scots spoke of the Good Neighbours or the Fair Folk and would not say fairies, lest by naming them openly they should draw upon themselves the notice of that people, and its anger.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Wherever mushrooms grew in a ring, men said, the Fair Folk had danced. A tale of Wales tells that Rhys danced in such a ring for months, and when his friend pulled him out he swore it had been but five minutes.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Mushrooms grow in a ring upon the stair: the Fair Folk are abroad on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Whenever a traveller of Devon or Cornwall was pixy-led, and went wandering astray in a field that he knew well, he would turn his coat inside out, for thus the spell was broken and he might find his way home.

abilities.name: Coat Turned Inside Out
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their confusion, sleep and charm.
abilities.trigger_msg: Coat Turned Inside Out: {The}'s glamour shimmers over you, but your coat is on inside out as the old wives counsel, and the magic slides away from you.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: A smith of the Highlands went into a fairy hill, so the tale runs, to win back his son, and he drove his dirk into the threshold, that the cold iron might keep the hill from closing behind him.

abilities.name: Cold Iron
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and 10% harder if it is iron or cold iron.
abilities.trigger_msg: Cold Iron! {The} shrieks as the iron bites, for the Fair Folk cannot bear its touch.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: The queen kept her child by guessing the name of the little man, which was Rumpelstiltskin. At this, say the brothers Grimm, he stamped his foot deep into the ground in his rage and tore himself in two.

abilities.name: Their True Name
abilities.text: Invisible or disguised Fair Folk within 4 tiles show to you, and their charm can never take you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Their True Name: you whisper the old name, and the air {where} ripples as a curtain does when it is drawn aside. {True_A} stands revealed!

great_beasts.name: Great Beasts
great_beasts.blurb: The great beasts are animals grown huge and savage, and among them is the quarry of all the old hunting tales. They have no magic but muscle, tooth and claw, and seldom do they need any other.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The peoples of the North so feared the bear that they would not speak his name. Thus the English 'bear' began, it may be, as 'the brown one', and the Slavic medved has the meaning 'honey-eater'.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Three creatures were the sign among the poets of Old English that blood would soon be shed, for the wolf, the raven and the eagle, the beasts of battle, gathered before the fighting and waited for their feast.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Fresh tracks and torn bark mark the stair: great beasts hunt this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Each day, as the Norse myths tell, the cook Andhrímnir boiled the boar Sæhrímnir to feed the warriors of Odin in Valhalla, and each evening the boar was made whole again.

abilities.name: Hunter's Harvest
abilities.text: Harvesting their corpses gives one extra portion.
abilities.trigger_msg: Hunter's Harvest: you know well where the best cuts lie, and take more than a common butcher would.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Heracles drove the Erymanthian Boar into deep snow until it floundered, and then he took it and bore it living to King Eurystheus, who was so greatly afraid that he hid himself in a jar of bronze.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: you watch the beast's shoulders and read its next move before it is made. You have longer to answer in this fight.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Androcles, as Aulus Gellius tells, was a runaway slave who drew a great splinter from the paw of a lion. When afterward he was thrown to the beasts in the Great Circus of Rome, he met that same lion, and it fawned upon him.

abilities.name: Beast-Friend
abilities.text: One lesser beast in ten arrives calm and leaves you be unless you strike first.
abilities.trigger_msg: Beast-Friend: the beasts here lift their heads to watch you, and knowing that you mean no harm they let you pass.

vermin.name: Vermin, Spiders and Swarms
vermin.blurb: In every crack of the dark dwell the small things that crawl and gnaw, spin and sting, often by the hundred. Alone they are but a nuisance, yet together they carry poison and plague, and the patient among them wait in silk.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Arachne the weaver, as Ovid tells, wove a flawless tapestry of the misdeeds of the gods, and Athena in her anger turned her into a spider. Her name is the Greek word for that creature, and spiders are called arachnids after it.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: When rats were found knotted by their tails, the folk named the knot a rat king and took it for an omen of plague, and one of 32 rats is kept mummified in a museum at Altenburg in Germany.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Webs and gnawed bones strew the stair, for vermin and spiders creep on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: The people of Apulia held that the bite of the tarantula must be danced out in wild tarantellas, sometimes for days together. Four thieves of Toulouse, says legend, robbed the victims of plague unharmed, being guarded by vinegar steeped in herbs.

abilities.name: Web and Plague
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their poison, disease, slowing and holding, and their poison and disease last a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Web and Plague: {The}'s bite stings, but you cleanse it at once, and the sickness takes no hold.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: A man who rested beside the water at Jōren Falls in Japan felt threads of silk winding about his leg, the legend says, and he slipped them onto the stump of a tree, which the jorōgumo spider straightway dragged into the falls.

abilities.name: Tremor-Sense
abilities.text: Vermin and spiders waiting in ambush within 4 tiles are revealed to you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Tremor-Sense: you feel the faintest tremor through the soles of your boots, for something is shifting in the rock {where}: {true_a}, lying in wait!

trigger_msg_if.msg: Tremor-Sense: you notice sticky, pale strands stretched across the passage {where}. A web! It trembles ever so slightly, and you spot {true_a} lying in wait on it!
Tremor-Sense: a fine trickle of grit falls from the ceiling {where}. You look up and see {true_a} clinging there, waiting to drop on you!

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: A piper in a coat of many colours came to Hamelin in 1284, says the legend, and led its rats into the River Weser with his tune. When the town cheated him of his fee he returned, and led away 130 of its children.

abilities.name: The Piper's Tune
abilities.text: A blow at chain 8 or more sends every lesser vermin and spider in sight fleeing for 5 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Piper's Tune! You whistle the tune of the piper of old, and the swarm turns and scurries away.

serpents.name: Serpents and Swamp-Kin
serpents.blurb: In the flooded halls dwell snakes both great and small, and with them the folk of scale and slime. They strike swiftly and their venom works slowly, and they lie coiled where you would least look for them.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Mucalinda the naga king, as Buddhist tradition tells, saw a great storm break over the Buddha in his meditation, and he wrapped him in seven coils and spread his hood above him for seven days.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: While Gilgamesh bathed in a pool, as his Epic tells, a snake stole from him the plant of rejuvenation, and as it glided away it cast its skin. From that hour, so the story seems to say, all serpents have renewed themselves.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: A shed skin lies on the stair: serpents coil on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: When Cleopatra died, by the bite of an asp as it was said, Octavian sent for the Psylli, a people of Libya thought to be proof against snakes, that they might draw out the venom, but they came too late.

abilities.name: Antivenom
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their poison and paralysis, and their poison lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Antivenom: {The}'s fangs sink in, but you chew the right herb at once, and the poison takes no hold.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: The ichneumon, which is the mongoose of Egypt, would roll again and again in the mud, so Pliny the Elder wrote, and let each coat bake hard in the sun, that it might go armoured to battle with the asp.

abilities.name: Mongoose
abilities.text: Your first blow in a fight against one starts at chain 2.
abilities.trigger_msg: Mongoose! You are swifter than {the}, and strike before {he} can.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: The Marsi of central Italy were said to descend from the son of Circe, and Pliny wrote that they could send snakes to sleep. At Cocullo, in their old land, the snake-catchers still drape the statue of Saint Dominic with living snakes every May 1.

abilities.name: Snake-Charmer
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, a lesser serpent you strike is charmed calm for 8 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Snake-Charmer: you sway with {the}, slow and steady, and {he} sways with you, calm for a little while.

birds.name: Birds and Winged Hunters
birds.blurb: The hunters of the air are some of them birds and some only birds in part. They dive at the eyes, and are away again before you can strike.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The great bird Simurgh found the babe Zal abandoned and reared him in her nest, as Ferdowsi sings in the Shahnameh. When he left her she gave him one of her feathers, that he might burn it and she would come.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Rome was founded by the omen of birds, for Remus saw six vultures and afterward Romulus saw twelve, and each brother claimed that the gods had chosen him.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Feathers drift down the stair from winged hunters that nest on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: It was the falconers of Arabia who first hooded their hawks, as the Emperor Frederick II wrote in the 1240s, and he took up the hood himself for its great usefulness, since a bird that is hooded will sit calm in the dark.

abilities.name: Hooded
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their blinding and confusion, as a falconer's hood calms a hawk.
abilities.trigger_msg: Hooded: {The} dives at your eyes, but you shield them in time and keep your head clear.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Drona set a bird in a tree for a target, as the Mahabharata relates, and asked his pupils what they saw. Arjuna alone answered that he saw nothing but its head, and his arrow struck the head away.

abilities.name: Falconer's Eye
abilities.text: Your bow and your thrown weapons hit them 5% harder.
abilities.trigger_msg: Falconer's Eye! You read {the}'s flight as a falconer would, lead your aim, and strike {him} hard.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Heracles could not come at the Stymphalian Birds in their marsh when he undertook his sixth labour, until Athena gave him rattles of bronze, the krotala that Hephaestus made, and at their clashing the birds rose in fear and he shot them.

abilities.name: Heracles' Rattle
abilities.text: At chain 12 or more, the din of your blow sends every lesser winged hunter in sight scattering for 6 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Heracles' Rattle! You clash your gear like the bronze rattle of Heracles, and the flock scatters in panic.

gorgons.name: Gorgons and Basilisks
gorgons.blurb: There are creatures whose mere look can stop the heart or turn living flesh to stone. The ancients lived through such meetings by never looking into their eyes.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The glaring face of the Gorgon, which is called the gorgoneion, was painted by the Greeks on shields and temple roofs and in the bottoms of their cups to frighten evil away, and Athena bore Medusa's head upon her aegis.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: All other serpents fled from the hiss of the basilisk, as Pliny wrote, and wherever it passed the grass was scorched and the stones were burst asunder.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Stone figures stand on the stair with faces frozen in fear, for a gorgon's gaze haunts this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Let no man meet the eyes of the basilisk, said the lore of the Middle Ages. Pliny named the weasel as its slayer, and in Cantabria in Spain those who travelled through its country carried a rooster, for the crowing was thought to be its death.

abilities.name: Averted Eyes
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their killing gaze and their poison.
abilities.trigger_msg: Averted Eyes: you keep your gaze on {the}'s feet and never on {his} face, and {his} stare cannot take you.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Perseus never looked upon Medusa, but watched her, as Apollodorus tells, in a shield of polished bronze while Athena guided his hand, and so he cut off her head as she slept.

abilities.name: Perseus' Shield
abilities.text: While you carry a shield, their gaze cannot take you at all.
abilities.trigger_msg: Perseus' Shield: you watch {the} only in the polished face of your shield, and {his} deadly gaze cannot reach you.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Hermes gave to Perseus the harpe, a sickle-sword of adamant, for the neck of Medusa. The lore of the Middle Ages added that a basilisk made to behold itself in a mirror would perish by its own stare.

abilities.name: Harpe
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and at chain 18 or more a lesser one below half health meets its own stare and turns to stone. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Harpe! Your curved blade bites deep into {the}'s neck, as Perseus' blade once did.

legend.name: Monsters of Legend
legend.blurb: By the slaying of these beasts the heroes won their fame, and each is the answer to an old tale. Most of them were overcome once before, by one who had learned the secret.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Flames of natural gas have burned from the rocks of Yanartaş, in Lycia in the land now called Turkey, for at least 2,500 years, and the place is also named the Chimaera, after the monster that breathed fire.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Every nine years, as Plutarch relates, Athens sent seven youths and seven maidens to the Minotaur, and their ship went out under a black sail, for all believed that they were voyaging to their deaths.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: An old tale is carved upon the stair, for a monster of legend waits on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Circe counselled Odysseus to row swiftly past the cliff of Scylla and offer no battle, since it were better to lose six men than all his ship to Charybdis. He held his course, and six of his men were taken.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: you know this tale and how it must end. You have longer to answer in this fight.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: As often as Heracles cut off a head of the Hydra two grew in its place, until his nephew Iolaus seared each stump with a burning brand, and thereafter the heads returned no more.

abilities.name: Iolaus' Torch
abilities.text: Your blows stop their regeneration for 3 turns, so a hydra's heads stay down.
abilities.trigger_msg: Iolaus' Torch: you sear {the}'s wound with fire, as Iolaus did for Heracles, and nothing grows again.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread to unwind as he went into the Labyrinth, and when he had killed the Minotaur he followed it back out of the maze that Daedalus had built to hold the beast.

abilities.name: Know the Story
abilities.text: Once per fight, your first wrong answer against one does not end your chain. You know how the story ends.
abilities.trigger_msg: Know the Story: you stumble on that answer, but you know how this tale goes and press on. Your chain holds this time!

shapeshifters.name: Werebeasts and Shapeshifters
shapeshifters.blurb: Some folk are not always folk, and there are animals that are not always animals. They hide in plain sight until the moon, or their hunger, or the chosen moment works the change upon them.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Herodotus had heard that among the Neuri, who dwelt beyond the Scythians, every one became a wolf for a few days in each year, but he confessed that the tale did not convince him.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: A wolf that raided a farmer's flock was speared in the neck, as Petronius tells in the Satyricon. On the morrow the soldier who had become a wolf the night before was found lying abed while a doctor tended his neck.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Claw-marks and a torn cloak lie on the stair: a shapeshifter hunts this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: The wolfsbane or aconite with which hunters poisoned wolves grew first, said the Greeks, from the drool of Cerberus when Heracles dragged him up from the underworld, and physicians of the Middle Ages even tried it as a cure for werewolves.

abilities.name: Wolfsbane
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their bleeding and disease, and their bleeding lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Wolfsbane: {The}'s bite tears your skin, but the wolfsbane that you carry keeps the curse from taking hold.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Jean Chastel slew the Beast of Gévaudan in 1767, and legend says that his bullet was silver. Historians trace that silver to novelists from 1935 onward, though German folk of the 19th century already held silver to be the werewolf's bane.

abilities.name: Silvered
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 3% harder, and 10% harder if it is silver.
abilities.trigger_msg: Silvered! {The} howls as the silver burns, for the shape {he} wears cannot endure it.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Menelaus held fast to Proteus the sea god, as the Odyssey tells, though he became a lion, a serpent, a leopard, a boar, running water and a tree, until Proteus was wearied and answered all that was asked of him.

abilities.name: Forced Shape
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, a lesser shapeshifter is stunned for 3 turns as its shape tears.
abilities.trigger_msg: Forced Shape! Your blow tears at {the}'s borrowed shape, and {he} staggers, caught halfway between two forms.

constructs.name: Golems and Constructs
constructs.blurb: Golems and their kind were never born, but made of stone, clay, bronze or clockwork and set walking by craft or magic. They feel neither pain nor fear, and they will obey their last command forever.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Hephaestus the smith of the gods made for himself handmaidens of gold, as Homer sings in the Iliad. They had the likeness of living girls, with minds and voices and strength, and they helped their lame master to walk.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: The brass head of Friar Bacon, in the old English tale, spoke at last while his servant Miles kept watch, saying 'Time is.' and 'Time was.' and 'Time is past.', but Miles never woke his master Bacon, and the head broke in pieces.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Stone grinds and brass ticks on the stair, for something made, not born, guards this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Rabbi Loew of Prague, the legend says, drew the shem, a slip that bore God's name, from the mouth of his golem each Friday, that it might rest on the Sabbath. But once he forgot, and it ran wild.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: constructs are slow and steady, and so are you. You have longer to answer in this fight.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Talos the giant of bronze was promised immortality by Medea, as Apollodorus tells, and then she drew out the bronze nail that stopped his single vein at the ankle, so that all his ichor gushed forth and he died.

abilities.name: Find the Seam
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, your blows ignore their resistances, as Medea pulled the nail from Talos's ankle.
abilities.trigger_msg: Find the Seam! You find the seam where {the}'s plates meet, and drive your blow home within it.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: The golem tales of Poland, and later of Prague, set emet, 'truth', upon the brow: rub away the first letter, leaving met, 'dead', and the golem falls. When Elijah of Chełm unmade his golem, it scarred him on the face.

abilities.name: Erase the Letter
abilities.text: At chain 18 or more, a lesser construct below 15% health falls lifeless: emet, truth, becomes met, dead. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Erase the Letter! You rub out one letter on {the}'s brow: emet, truth, becomes met, dead. {He} crashes to the ground.

elementals.name: Elementals and Djinn
elementals.blurb: The elementals are living fire, stone, wind and water, and spirits of smokeless flame. They are the raw stuff of the world, and quick to wrath.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: All things are made of four roots, earth and water and air and fire: so taught Empedocles the Greek. Legend says that he leapt at last into Mount Etna, and that the mountain cast back one of his sandals of bronze.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: The blue flames that danced upon the mastheads in storms were named St. Elmo's fire by the seamen, and the sailors of ancient Greece beheld in a pair of such lights the twins Castor and Pollux, a sign that they should pass in safety.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The air of the stair tastes of lightning and ash, for elementals stir on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: So cold was the salamander, as Pliny claimed, that it quenched fire by its touch. In later days asbestos, which will not burn, was taken for salamander's hair, and the fabled Prester John was said to own a robe of it.

abilities.name: Ward of the Elements
abilities.text: Their fire, cold, lightning and acid hurt you 5% less.
abilities.trigger_msg: Ward of the Elements: {The} lashes out with raw elemental force, but you meet it as you were taught, and it hurts you less.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: To each element, as Aristotle taught, belong two qualities: fire is hot and dry, water cold and wet, air hot and wet, and earth cold and dry, so that fire and water have none in common.

abilities.name: Opposing Element
abilities.text: Your blows hit 6% harder when they strike what the elemental is weak to.
abilities.trigger_msg: Opposing Element! You answer {the} with the one element that {he} cannot bear, and {he} reels.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: A fisherman once drew up in his net a copper jar shut with the seal of Solomon, as it is told in The Fisherman and the Jinni, and out of it poured a furious jinni, whom he tricked back within by asking how it could ever have fitted there.

abilities.name: Solomon's Seal
abilities.text: Their burning and freezing wear off twice as fast, and their elemental damage hurts you 10% less.
abilities.trigger_msg: Solomon's Seal: you trace the seal of Solomon in the air, and the elemental's hold on you grows weaker.

oozes.name: Oozes and Slimes
oozes.blurb: Without mind or shape, these eaters creep through the dungeon and strip it of all that is soft. Whatever they touch is dissolved, and to cut the wrong one only makes more of it.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Lumps of jelly have been found upon the grass of Britain since at least the 1300s and blamed upon shooting stars, and the shepherds of Wales named the stuff pwdre ser, 'rot of the stars'.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: The nuppeppō of Japanese lore is a wandering lump of flesh with a face among its folds, and it shuffles by night through the empty streets with the reek of rotting meat about it.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair is slick and smells of acid, for oozes creep on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: A yellow jelly upon the gate, which was called witches' butter, warned the folk of Germany and Scandinavia that a witch had cursed the house, and they believed that to prick it with pins of metal broke the spell.

abilities.name: Clean Blade
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their paralysis and weakness, and their weakness lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Clean Blade: {The}'s slime splashes you, but you wipe it away before it can numb your limbs.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Every drop of the demon Raktabija's blood that touched the earth rose up as another Raktabija, as the Devi Mahatmya tells, and therefore the goddess Kali drank the blood as it flowed, before ever a drop could fall.

abilities.name: Strike True
abilities.text: Your blows never split them, and your weapon hits them 5% harder.
abilities.trigger_msg: Strike True! You strike so cleanly that {the} cannot split in two.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Steve, whom Steve McQueen played in the 1958 film The Blob, discovered that the creature could not endure the cold. The townsfolk froze it with fire extinguishers, and the Air Force bore it away through the sky to the Arctic.

abilities.name: Fire and Frost
abilities.text: Your blows hit 10% harder when they strike what an ooze is weak to.
abilities.trigger_msg: Fire and Frost! {The} shrivels and hisses beneath the blow.

aberrations.name: Aberrations
aberrations.blurb: There are things that ought never to have been: minds from beyond the stars, eyes that float and mouths that wait. They war upon the mind as much as upon the body, and many of them are other than they seem.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: So vast was the kraken of Norway, wrote Bishop Erik Pontoppidan in 1752, that its back was mistaken for islands. It may be that the giant squid, which was first photographed alive in 2004, lies behind the tale.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Sailors who landed on the risen city of R'lyeh, in H. P. Lovecraft's The Call of Cthulhu, found all its angles wrong, and one man was swallowed by an angle that was acute and yet behaved as though it were obtuse.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair feels wrong and seems to bend, for aberrations lurk on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Odysseus, in the Odyssey, stopped the ears of his crew with beeswax and bade them bind him to the mast, that he might hear the Sirens, and when he begged to be loosed they bound him the tighter.

abilities.name: Steel Mind
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their confusion and paralysis, and their hallucinations last a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steel Mind: {The} claws at your thoughts, but you hold fast to what is real, and the attack on your mind fails.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: When a tool has lasted a hundred years, the Japanese tales say, it may awaken as a living tsukumogami. A medieval scroll tells of old tools cast out before that day was come, which awoke none the less, and were full of spite.

abilities.name: Mimic-Sense
abilities.text: A disguised mimic within 2 tiles gives itself away to you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Mimic-Sense: a shadow {where} does not move as shadows should. You look more closely: {true_a} is lying in wait!

trigger_msg_if.msg: Mimic-Sense: something {where} looks just a little wrong. Its edges are too soft, and it seems to breathe. It is {true_a}, waiting for you to touch it!
Mimic-Sense: the stone {where} is too smooth and too even, as if it were stretched over something. It is {true_a}, waiting for you to step onto it!

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Argus the giant had a hundred eyes and never closed them all at once, so that nothing could steal past him, until Hermes charmed him to sleep and slew him, and Hera set his eyes in the tail of the peacock.

abilities.name: The Unblinking
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and their ambushers never catch you unawares.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Unblinking! You never look away from {the}, and your blow lands the harder for it.

plants.name: Plants and Fungi
plants.blurb: The growths of the dungeon spring up green and grey where nothing should grow, as mould and vine and walking rot. They cannot pursue you far, and so they draw you to them, or lay you asleep where you stand.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The New York World printed in 1874 the account of a German botanist who had seen a man-eating tree in Madagascar. It was all the invention of the reporter Edmund Spencer, yet explorers went seeking that tree for many years afterward.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Macbeth was promised by a vision of the witches, in Shakespeare's play, that he was safe until Birnam Wood should come to Dunsinane, and then a messenger beheld the forest moving, for soldiers bore its cut boughs before them.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Spores drift like dust on the stair, for something green and hungry grows on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: The plague doctors of the 1600s went about in beaked masks stuffed with lavender, peppermint, cloves and myrrh, for they believed that sweet scents would ward off the evil air by which sickness was thought to travel.

abilities.name: Herbalist's Mask
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their poison, sleep and hallucinations, and their poison lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Herbalist's Mask: {The} puffs a cloud of spores at you, but you breathe through your mask, and they take no hold.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: The mandrake, said the lore of the Middle Ages, shrieked when it was pulled and killed all who heard. Therefore the gatherers tied it to a dog to be dragged free, a craft that Josephus described in the first century.

abilities.name: Herbalist
abilities.text: Harvesting them gives one extra portion.
abilities.trigger_msg: Herbalist: you know which parts of a plant are worth the keeping, and gather more than most would.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Boniface laid his axe about the year 723 to Donar's Oak at Geismar, a tree holy to Thor. A blast from above helped to overthrow it, as his biographer tells, and Boniface built a chapel of its timber.

abilities.name: Woodsman's Axe
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and their ambushers never catch you unawares.
abilities.trigger_msg: Woodsman's Axe! You hew {the} low, just where {he} grows from the ground.

celestials.name: Celestials
celestials.blurb: The celestials are servants of heaven and of the gods, some pure still and some fallen into evil. Their light is blinding and their purpose is fixed, and they seldom begin a quarrel.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The horn of the unicorn was once believed in Europe to discover poison, and kings held it very precious. Most such horns were the tusks of narwhals, of which the throne of Denmark's coronations was built in the 1660s.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Shepherds were watching their flock by night, as the Gospel of Luke relates, when an angel appeared and the glory of the Lord shone round them, and they were sore afraid. The first words that the angel spoke were 'Fear not.'

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: A clean light falls on the stair, for a celestial creature walks this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: The face of Moses so shone after Sinai, says Exodus, that the Israelites feared to come near him, and he covered it with a veil. Among the Greeks it was told that Semele beheld Zeus in his full glory and died.

abilities.name: Shaded Eyes
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their blinding and confusion.
abilities.trigger_msg: Shaded Eyes: {The}'s blinding light flares, but you look past it rather than into it, and keep your sight.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: The Israelites marked their doorposts with the blood of a lamb, as Exodus tells, and when the destroyer came for the firstborn of Egypt the Lord passed over every door so marked.

abilities.name: Angel's Due
abilities.text: Their holy damage hurts you 5% less.
abilities.trigger_msg: Angel's Due: {The}'s holy fire pours down, but you bow your head in reverence, and it passes over you.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Abraham set food before three strangers at Mamre, as Genesis tells, and they proved to be visitors from heaven. Ovid tells how old Baucis and Philemon fed Jupiter and Mercury in disguise, and richly were those hosts rewarded.

abilities.name: Entertaining Angels
abilities.text: One lesser celestial in five arrives calm and leaves you be unless you strike first.
abilities.trigger_msg: Entertaining Angels: the beings of light look upon you here and let you be.

grave_watch.name: The Grave Watch

boon.name: Vigil
boon.text: Necrotic and draining damage hurt you 5% less, from any source.

grave_watch.chronicle: Know every kind of the dead. Can keep watch on a grave all night.

wild_road.name: The Wild Road

boon.name: Ranger's Instinct
boon.text: You see one tile further in the dark.

wild_road.chronicle: Know the wild things of the dark. Can walk their roads like a ranger.

hellward_gate.name: The Hellward Gate

boon.name: Unbent Mind
boon.text: You get +1 on every saving throw against confusion, charm and fear, from anything.

hellward_gate.chronicle: Learned the tricks of all that creep into a mind. Mine bends no more.

heroes_road.name: The Hero's Road

boon.name: Hero's Nerve
boon.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock against any boss.

heroes_road.chronicle: Know the old stories. Can walk the road the heroes walked.

loremaster.title: Loremaster
loremaster.chronicle: Know five families of monster to the last weakness. A loremaster now.
